clue.text: Consecrated small area of land to dead

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an acre is a unit of land area
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A little plot of ground blessed for burying the dead, like a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consecrated has been made holy, and sacred is a direct synonym meaning set apart for worship.

clue.text: Meagreness of local shops takes character away from town

parts.note: Spar is a chain of small neighbourhood convenience stores in Britain, so several local shops are Spars

indicators.note: taking a character away means one letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: a large town, loosely a city

explanation.surface: A town's lack of corner shops shows how thin its amenities are.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a British chain of convenience stores. The character taken away is the town's own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsity is thinness or scantiness of supply, a close synonym for meagreness.

clue.text: Increasing gloom caught couple climbing amidst heather

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: amidst places one piece in the middle of another word

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a duo is a couple, a pair

explanation.surface: A walker caught on the moor as the weather closes in over the heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is a less familiar name for heather; the couple climbs because this is a down clue, then sits amidst it, with the cricket abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouding over describes a sky or mood growing darker, so it is gloom on the increase.

clue.text: Often nuisance calls are made out of boredom

indicators.note: made out of says the answer is built from the run of letters in the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Cold callers who pester people are often just bored themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across oftEN NUIsance; 'calls' is part of the hiding phrase rather than the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for listless weariness, the same as boredom.

clue.text: Angry suitor reported to have weapon

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the word is chosen for its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a beau is a suitor, and is said like the archer's bow

explanation.surface: A furious rejected admirer is said to be armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow firing bolts, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Ride wave on merchant ship

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy sea wave
a coaster is a trading vessel that sails along the coast

explanation.surface: Riding a big wave aboard a cargo vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollercoaster is a fairground attraction, an example of a ride.

clue.text: Terrible crew first killed after vessel caused disaster at sea

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows the vessel word

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are in a bad, disordered state
first means only the opening letter of killed is used

explanation.surface: A dreadful crew were the first to die when their ship met catastrophe on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwreck is the destruction or sinking of a ship, a calamity at sea.

clue.text: Crash is end of fine run for old car

parts.note: a bang is the noise of a crash

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of fine
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A collision ends an old car's good stretch of driving.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a banger is a battered old car (it is also a sausage).
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is informal British slang for a dilapidated old motor car.

clue.text: Wife managed tear at husband's funeral tribute

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: managed suggests handled and rearranged, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: the letters of tear rearranged
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A widow holds back only a single tear at her husband's burial.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of flowers is laid at a funeral as a tribute to the dead.

clue.text: Trouble with sailors on deck

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors having bother up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but it is the verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something out is to decorate it, which is what adorn means.

clue.text: Flirtation is key to marriage

parts.note: D is a musical key
a marriage is an alliance between two people or families

explanation.surface: A wry claim that a little flirting is the secret of a happy marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic involvement, the same idea as a flirtation.

clue.text: Rosetta died in storm at sea

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also serves in the signal

explanation.surface: A woman named Rosetta was lost when a storm struck her ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' is part of the shipwreck picture but means confused.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at sea is an idiom for being bewildered, which is being disorientated.

clue.text: Border dispute distracts from main point

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what the noun answer does

parts.note: a side is an edge or border
an issue is a matter in dispute

explanation.surface: A frontier quarrel diverts attention from the real matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary topic that pulls attention away from the central question.

clue.text: Force woman to take break

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for woman
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Making a woman stop for a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to obtain by force, twisting something away from someone.

clue.text: Players tackle Wimbledon crowd noise?

parts.note: Wimbledon is the famous London tennis championship
a racket is a din, like a noisy crowd

explanation.surface: Players dealing with a rowdy crowd at the All England Club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb but is the noun for equipment; the question mark flags the loose Wimbledon-for-tennis substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle means gear or equipment, and a racket is the gear tennis players use.

clue.text: Landlord in Newcastle has to live off beer

parts.note: split as new (N, its abbreviation) and castle (KEEP, a castle's stronghold)

indicators.note: off means the following word is taken away from the beer

parts.note: taken as written, before the removal
to be means to exist, to live

explanation.surface: A Geordie publican survives by drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Newcastle as new (N) plus castle (KEEP); BE taken from BEER leaves ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs an inn or pub, the job of a landlord in British usage.

clue.text: Utter a sob when moved by old instrument

indicators.note: when moved means the letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: the lute is a stringed instrument of earlier centuries

explanation.surface: Someone lets out a sob when stirred by an old musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like the verb 'say', but it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and utter both mean complete or total, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Chose Leeds building to accommodate city culture centre

indicators.note: to accommodate means the anagram holds the other letters inside
building means the letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: the centre of culture is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Leeds development was picked to house an arts centre for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC and T go into the middle of the rearranged LEEDS: SEL + ECT + ED. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To have selected is to have chosen or picked out from a range.

clue.text: Translation of rune symbol by expert reveals nothing special

indicators.note: a translation renders the word in another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mark is a symbol or sign
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: An expert deciphers a runic sign and finds it nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unremarkable is ordinary and not worth comment, with nothing special about it.

clue.text: Restaurant cooked ribs to order

indicators.note: cooked suggests mixing up, so the letters are altered
putting things into a new order underlines the rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner where ribs are prepared fresh when you ask.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, originally French.

clue.text: Young scout's first off into Scandinavian river

indicators.note: into places one piece inside another

parts.note: a Dane is someone from Denmark

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a Cub is a junior member of the Scouts

explanation.surface: A young scout falling into a river in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: Cub is the name for a junior Scout, and 'first off' removes its opening letter before the remainder sits inside the Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river flowing to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Angry tirade spoiled day out

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters are disordered
out means a letter leaves the word

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A furious rant ruined a family outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lead part of roof takes time to position

indicators.note: takes means the word holds another piece inside it

parts.note: a tile is one piece of a roof
T is the abbreviation for time
a role is a position or function

explanation.surface: Lead sheeting on part of a roof is slow to fit into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal used on roofs; it is the leading part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role is the character a play or film is named after, usually the lead part.

clue.text: More mature tree

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small tree bearing elderflowers and berries

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of old in family senses and the name of a small tree with dark berries.

clue.text: Don't start to play guitar, Mr Gabriel — be a brass player!

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings
Peter Gabriel is the English rock singer, once of Genesis

explanation.surface: Advice to the rock star Peter Gabriel to drop guitar for the horn section.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter plays the trumpet, a brass instrument.

clue.text: Alarm a bit over peacekeepers being brought in

indicators.note: brought in means one piece is put inside another
over means turned back, so the word reads right to left

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
UN troops are international peacekeepers

explanation.surface: A little worry about UN troops arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alarm' could be a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt is to intimidate or dishearten, so to alarm.

clue.text: Disregard mistake in Roman poet's English

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another word

parts.note: Ovid is the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
to err is to make a mistake
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Ignoring an error in an English version of a Latin poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s in 'poet's' links the poet to the English that follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: To override is to set aside or overrule, which is to disregard.

clue.text: Father and I meet close mate

parts.note: Fr is the title abbreviation for a priest, Father
taken as written
the close is the end

explanation.surface: A priest and the speaker get together with a close pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as an adjective with mate but is the noun meaning end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British for a pal, which is a friend.
